scope: Full-frame raw DROID SVO/HDF5 to SequenceExample/LeRobot alignment for held-out episodes 21 and 77
summary: All six real camera streams pass full-frame pixel identity, adjacent-shift discrimination, one-terminal-row, and constant timestamp-offset gates, completing the raw-to-LeRobot lineage chain for episodes 21 and 77.
evidence: The audit ran on strictly free physical A800 GPU 6 and returned accepted=true with alignment SHA-256 f1840fdf70a4729936aba18f46404e3871dcd1d3c9fcf03943dd098664c9a9a5.
Episode 21 maps 92 SVO/SequenceExample frames to 93 HDF5 rows; episode 77 maps 100 frames to 101 rows, proving one excluded terminal HDF5 row in each case.
Across six cameras, raw-SVO-to-SequenceExample PSNR p05 spans 27.037-35.264 dB and dHash p95 spans 1-3 bits, passing frozen 25 dB and 8-bit gates.
Same-index median PSNR beats the best adjacent-frame shift by 1.999-11.224 dB across all cameras.
SVO-minus-HDF5 timestamp offset medians are 41.416-41.538 ms, with centered residual p95 only 0.459-0.529 ms.
The terminal HDF5 row follows the last SVO frame by 8.226-42.168 ms.
Episode-local exterior assignments remain explicit: raw exterior_1 maps to LeRobot exterior_image_2_left and raw exterior_2 maps to exterior_image_1_left for both episodes.
The accepted SequenceExample-to-LeRobot manifest is hash-bound, so raw_svo_to_sequence_pixels_verified, raw_hdf5_to_sequence_timing_verified, and raw_to_lerobot_chain_verified are all true.
lessons: The apparent frame mismatch is a single terminal HDF5 control row, not missing SVO video.
A stable approximately 41.5 ms acquisition offset is measurable and must be preserved rather than silently zeroed.
Same-index versus adjacent-frame evidence is necessary to rule out an off-by-one match in slowly moving robot video.
limitations: Episode 60 remains absent from the public raw bucket.
Official raw DROID training and redistribution rights remain unresolved.
Lineage/calibration does not establish novel-view generation quality.
next_actions: Use the verified episodes 21/77 camera chains for geometry-conditioned novel-view validation.
Do not use raw DROID for claim-eligible training until rights are resolved.
